findings.claim: The whole G1 argument, and the scheduler risks used for STATUS and POS, assume the pinned runtime loads `work/rounds/R-0007/tasks/*.json`. It does not. In `release-host.js`, `tasksDir` (187162) returns `.devai/state/tasks`, and `loadTask`/`listTasks` (187202–187214) read only that folder. `runRoundTasks` (188643), `roundTaskStatus` and `taskDependencies` get their tasks from there. `plan.md:61` itself says `.devai/state/tasks/` does not exist. So without a seal, `start/finish/escalate/pause/resume` on S2/S3 already fail with 'task not found', and `round status` returns 0 tasks. The negative test in step 2 of the G1 sequence would pass even without a seal, so it proves nothing. The rehearsal also never ran an unsealed baseline in the clone. Only `materializeRoundQueueTask` (188269) can write a TASK into the runtime store, and it is already behind the round guard. The dispatch path this repository really used, `tools/orchestra/worker.sh` (see R-0014 B3), reads prompts directly and does not go through `close-state.jsonl`. The 'Limite' paragraph mentions only a generic 'script/CLI externo'. As written, the Owner is asked to approve a sequence exception to CTG-0003 against a threat that has not been shown to exist.
findings.fix: State which runtime path actually reads the round's TASK files and cite `tasksDir`/`listTasks`. Add an unsealed baseline to the clone rehearsal so the rejection can be compared before and after the seal. Show a concrete way an archival TASK could be dispatched (materialize, worker.sh, maestro), or present G1 as defense-in-depth with its real benefit and cost. Name `tools/orchestra/worker.sh` as unguarded. Reassess whether STATUS=S1 needs G1/G2 at all or only a static no-dispatch check in `verify:round-tasks` plus the operational ban.
